chunks: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower.

key_terms.تُزِغْ: Cause to deviate or turn aside

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when we ask God not to make our hearts deviate after guiding us?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often recited by the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful to seek stability in faith (thabat) after the initial bestowal of guidance, emphasizing that continued steadfastness is a divine gift rather than merely human effort. It highlights the necessity of divine mercy (rahmah) to prevent the heart from swerving (zagh) due to worldly distractions or internal desires, affirming God’s attribute as Al-Wahhab, the Bestower of Gifts.
